components.name: Capacity Gauge
components.description: Read-only remaining-capacity gauge with a restrained four-stop semantic gradient.

narrative.overview: CodexStatus feels like a compact native instrument viewed through a thin, luminous material. Cyan, rose, apricot, and a trace of violet appear as large refracted volumes behind the interface; they never become text effects or decorative outlines. Light mode is clear and softly luminous. Dark mode is transparent black glass with restrained, low-luminance color pools—not a whitened or grey frosted card.
keyCharacteristics: Real Acrylic/DirectComposition translucency with an opaque accessibility fallback.
Large ambient color fields rather than rainbow borders or gradient text.
Compact native density and unchanged product semantics.

rules.name: Color-Belongs-to-Material
rules.body: Aurora color may live behind glass, in the capacity gauge, or in small semantic cues; never place it inside headline or quota-number glyphs.

rules.name: Flat-Type
rules.body: Text uses solid fills only—no glow, bloom, gradient fill, or colored outline.

rules.name: Black-Glass
rules.body: Dark surfaces must remain visibly black; increasing translucency must never be simulated by adding a milky grey veil.

dos: Do keep the quota number neutral and let the percent mark and gauge carry status.
Do test light, dark, high-contrast, disabled-transparency, and GDI fallback states.
Do keep Aurora volumes broad, soft, and subordinate to data.
donts: Don't apply gradients, glow, bloom, or chromatic outlines to text.
Don't whiten dark glass into grey fog.
Don't add a slider thumb, endpoint dot, or heavy bevel to the read-only capacity gauge.
Don't stack multiple opaque glass cards until the desktop context disappears.
